content:
Quick answer: Pets can offer companionship, but arthritis can make lifting, feeding, walking and cleaning harder. Adapt tasks and arrange backup care so both you and your pet are safe.

Choosing manageable routines

Think about your mobility, energy, finances and the pet's exercise and care needs. A pet that requires frequent lifting or strong leash control may not be a good fit during painful flares.

Reducing strain at home

Use lightweight food containers, accessible storage and stable feeding arrangements. Consider long-handled cleaning tools and divide tasks into short periods.

Walking and handling

Wear supportive footwear and use a lead you can control without pulling on painful joints. Ask for help with larger dogs if balance, grip or mobility are affected.

Planning for flare-ups

Identify a trusted person or pet-care service for walks, appointments and urgent care. Ask an occupational therapist about everyday task adaptations when pain affects independence.
